text:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming route /v1/generate-stream p99 > SLO (configured p99=1200ms). paging oncall
Mia (oncall-sre): I'm oncall — acknowledging. tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform. starting triage.
Ben (eng-runtime): pulling traces now. initial numbers: p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~4.6s over last 5m. throughput normal. tail increase looks concentrated on chunked responses.
Charlie (eng-platform): seeing related spikes at the proxy layer: nginx upstream write_timeouts jumping, lots of EAGAIN in proxy logs.
Ava (support): we got 6 customer reports in the last 10m: UI spinner, aborted streaming sessions. two high-traffic customers (acme-corp, beta-app) impacted.
Mia (oncall-sre): scope: streaming stalls / chunking delays. customer impact = degraded UX, some aborts. severity: P1-ish since p99 SLO breached and multiple customers affected.
Ben (eng-runtime): quick dump of per-request timings:
```
route: /v1/generate-stream
last5m p50 120ms p95 1.2s p99 4.6s
most tail events show large gaps between chunks (10s+ in some cases)
```
Ben (eng-runtime): adding logs: pattern = clients with very small recv-window (slow consumers) + large KV-cache misses causing runtime backpressure.
Charlie (eng-platform): nginx logs show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream". also running out of worker buffers.
Omar (eng-infra): checking node metrics — one host in the pool shows elevated kernel retransmits and high tcp_outnext_seq; could be kernel sendq piling.
Mia (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations we can try (order):
  1) enable proxy streaming-fallback to short-poll for affected routes (reduces chunking pressure)
  2) bump nginx `proxy_send_timeout` and `proxy_buffering` to avoid premature timeouts while we stabilize
  3) deploy temporary per-connection throttling to avoid single slow consumer hogging resources
  4) if needed, restart a small subset of proxy pods behind the LB (rolling)
Ben (eng-runtime): I'm going to disable request-level batching for /v1/generate-stream (experimental) to reduce head-of-line stalls and flush smaller chunks more frequently. doing it now.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: eng-runtime/disable-stream-batching -> canary 3 pods.
Ben (eng-runtime): canary up. early telemetry: p95 down to 800ms on canary, p99 1.6s for canary traffic. promising.
Charlie (eng-platform): applying `proxy_buffering off` and increasing `proxy_send_timeout` from 60s -> 120s on the affected proxy group. also enabling `proxy_max_temp_file_size 0` to bypass temp files.
Omar (eng-infra): live kernel tweak: increasing net.core.wmem_max and net.core.rmem_max on proxy nodes for extra socket buffers, will roll across 4 nodes.
Ava (support): telling customers we're investigating and applyng mitigations; advising them to retry streams if they see stalls.
Mia (oncall-sre): collecting telemetry: after mitigations (10m), cluster p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.2s — still borderline but much improved from 4.6s. some residual tail events remain.
Ben (eng-runtime): dug into runtime logs — noticed periodic GC pauses in a helper process responsible for chunk serialization (not the main model process). GC coincides with long gaps between chunks.
Charlie (eng-platform): interesting — proxy timeouts + slow consumer + periodic GC = amplified tail. suggest two-pronged: short-term proxy/workarounds, mid-term fix to avoid heavy GC during streaming.
Ben (eng-runtime): prepared a patch to move chunk serialization off the GC-heavy thread (PR ready). will schedule post-incident rollout.
Mia (oncall-sre): next action items:
  - keep canary running for 30m, observe p99.
  - Omar continue node buffer roll.
  - Ben ship GC-thread patch to staging and test with long-lived streams.
  - Charlie follow up on nginx tuning docs and add circuit-breaker for slow-consumers.
  - Support notify customers of mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution.
product-ops: customer-impact note: flag accounts with >3 aborted streams in last 15m for outreach.
Ben (eng-runtime): telemetry at +22m: p95 420ms p99 980ms. still seeing rare 8-12s gaps for a tiny fraction (~0.02%) of streams. investigating socket-level retransmits on those sessions.
Charlie (eng-platform): created temporary LB policy to move heavy streaming connections to a newly provisioned pool with higher buffer limits. starting traffic migration.
Mia (oncall-sre): handoff: I'll remain on until p99 < 900ms for 30m or until Ben/Charlie sign off. Omar, can you take over if this persists past the hour?
Omar (eng-infra): I can take follow-up. Will monitor kernel metrics and finish buffer roll.
Ben (eng-runtime): noted actionable root causes: slow consumers + GC on serialization thread + proxy buffer configuration. long-term: (1) move chunk serialization to non-GC path, (2) add backpressure/circuit-breaker for slow-consumers, (3) improve proxy defaults for streaming.
Mia (oncall-sre): logging timeline + actions to incident tracker. potential follow-up: postmortem to include customer impact metrics and coordinated rollout plan for the serialization fix.
Ava (support): I'll send a proactive message to impacted customers with apologies and a summary of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.
Ben (eng-runtime): creating PR: "runtime: offload chunk serialization to io-worker" -> link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/+/12345
Charlie (eng-platform): added nginx tuning doc snippet to infra-runbook: `streaming-proxy-tuning.md`
Mia (oncall-sre): marking incident as "mitigation in progress". will update if p99 regresses. thanks team. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deployment completed successfully.
Mia (oncall-sre): 28m after start: cluster p95 400ms p99 750ms. Handing off monitoring to Omar. If p99 climbs >1.2s again, page SRE and reopen.
Omar (eng-infra): ack, monitoring and alerts set. next update in 30m or on regression.
product-ops: noted for stakeholder comms.
Mia (oncall-sre): closing the slack triage thread; formal postmortem to be scheduled. thanks again everyone.
